transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me today, I really do appreciate it. I, um... well, I suppose I'm here because I'm just having a bit of a hard time keeping on top of things lately. I hope it's alright that I came in for this. 

You see, my wife had a fall recently, and... well, I've always been the organized one. The man with the lists and the plan, you know? But since it happened, I just... I don't know what's wrong with me. I've gone from managing everything to just sitting at the kitchen table, staring blankly at her medication chart. 

It’s quite embarrassing to admit out loud, actually, but I’ve been getting tearful, or snapping over absolutely nothing. And I'm letting everything else go—the bills, my mentoring calls, even just basic housework. It’s all just piling up, and I feel terrible because I just can't seem to make myself function the way I should be. I really want to be doing better for her. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining things properly and that I'm in the right place.
How long have you been feeling this way since your wife's fall?

Well, let's see... it's been about two months now. Yes, right around two months since the fall. I know it sounds like quite a long time to let things slide, and I really should have gotten a handle on it by now, shouldn't I? I mean, I keep thinking I'll wake up tomorrow and be back to my old self, but... well, it's just been two months of this, ever since everything at home changed. I hope I haven't waited too long to come in and see you about it. Is two months a normal amount of time to struggle with something like this?
Have you been enjoying the things you normally like to do since your wife's fall?

Oh, um... well, I suppose I haven't really thought about it. I certainly don't want to sound like I'm complaining or being entirely gloomy, you know? I do still enjoy my usual hobbies. I just... well, I haven't really been doing them as much lately, mostly because I've been so preoccupied with my wife's care and, well, trying to get myself organized. 

But I'm quite sure the enjoyment is still there. I think if I actually sat down to do them, I'd like them just fine. I just haven't really had the time or the focus to notice, to be completely honest. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering that properly for you.
Are there things that you used to enjoy doing that you no longer find pleasure in?

Well, no, not really. I mean, I don't think so. As I was saying, I think I would still enjoy my usual things if I just made the time for them. I certainly haven't lost interest in life or anything dreadful like that. 

I suppose I just haven't been doing my crossword puzzles or tending to the garden quite as much, but that's only because I need to be available for my wife, isn't it? It wouldn't be right of me to be out pruning the roses when she might need help getting to the bathroom. So, no, I wouldn't say I've stopped finding pleasure in things, I've just... reprioritized, I suppose. That's the right way to handle a situation like this, isn't it? Putting her needs first? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing.
Do you often feel guilty about things that have happened since your wife's fall?

Guilty? Oh, um... well, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I certainly hope I haven't given myself any reason to feel guilty! I've been trying so very hard to do everything exactly right for her since she came home. Making sure she's comfortable, keeping track of her appointments... I'm really giving it my absolute all. 

I suppose anyone might wish they could have somehow stopped an accident from happening in the first place, but... well, I know I can't blame myself for her slipping, can I? That wouldn't be very sensible. So, no, I don't feel guilty. I just try to focus entirely on being a good husband to her now. 

I hope that doesn't sound, oh, callous or unfeeling of me? I just think dwelling on guilt wouldn't be of any use to her, and I really do want to be as helpful and supportive as possible. I'm looking at it the right way, aren't I?
Have you lost any weight since your wife's fall?

Weight? Oh, um... no, I don't believe I have. I haven't actually stepped on a scale recently, to be perfectly honest, but my trousers all seem to fit exactly the same as they always have. 

I've been making quite sure to keep up with my meals. I know it wouldn't do my wife any good at all if I let my own health slip, would it? I really need to keep my strength up so I can be of use to her. So, no, no weight loss. I hope that's a good sign? I suppose it means I'm managing things reasonably well, doesn't it?
Have you been experiencing any feelings of restlessness or anxiety since your wife's fall?

Anxiety? Oh... well, I wouldn't want to use a strong word like that. It makes it sound as though I'm falling apart, and I really am trying so hard to keep everything together for her. But... well, I suppose I have been feeling a bit overwhelmed, if I'm being completely honest. I feel rather dreadful admitting it to you. 

You see, I've always been the man with the lists and the plan. Very organized, always on top of things. But lately... I just find myself sitting at the kitchen table, staring blankly at her medication chart for ages. And I might... well, I might suddenly start crying, or I'll snap over absolutely nothing at all, which I feel terrible about. She doesn't deserve that from me. 

I've even let things slide, which really isn't like me. The bills, my mentoring calls, even just basic housework... they're all just piling up. It's almost like I just can't make myself function properly right now. But... well, that's just a normal adjustment period, isn't it? It doesn't mean I'm failing her as a caregiver, does it? I'm sure if I just try a little harder, I'll get back on track. That's the right way to look at it, surely?
Are there things or situations that you've been avoiding since your wife's fall?

Avoiding things? Oh, um... no, I don't believe so. I mean, I certainly haven't been going out to my usual club meetings or seeing friends quite as much, but... well, that's definitely not because I'm avoiding them or anything of that sort! It's simply because my place is right here at home with her. 

I just want to be absolutely sure I'm available the moment she needs me. So, while I suppose I haven't been out and about, it's purely out of dedication to her care, not because I'm hiding away from the world or avoiding situations. I wouldn't want you to think I was just shutting myself away out of fear. 

It's the proper thing to do, isn't it, staying close by while she recovers? I just want to make sure I'm prioritizing her needs exactly the way a good husband should. That's the right approach, don't you agree?
Do you feel sad most of the day?

Sad? Oh, goodness, no. No, I wouldn't say that at all. I know I admitted earlier to... well, to tearing up sometimes, which I still feel perfectly awful about, but I certainly don't spend my days moping around. That wouldn't be very helpful of me, would it? 

I really make a point to put on a brave face and keep things as cheerful as possible for her. She’s the one who had the terrible fall, after all, so it would be terribly selfish of me to sit around feeling sorry for myself. I try to just focus on the positive and keep her spirits up. That’s really the most important thing a husband can do right now, don't you think? I certainly wouldn't want you to think I was just wallowing in it all. Staying upbeat is the best medicine for her, surely?
Do you feel emotionally distant from things or people that normally matter to you?

Emotionally distant? Oh, dear, no. No, I wouldn't say that at all. If anything, I feel... well, perhaps I feel things a bit too sharply right now. 

I know I mentioned earlier that I haven't been keeping up with my mentoring calls or seeing my friends, but... well, I still care about them very deeply! I haven't stopped caring or detached from them in any way. It's just that all my emotional energy is being poured directly into my wife's recovery at the moment. I feel so completely invested in making sure she's comfortable and safe. 

I would absolutely hate for you to think I was growing cold or pulling away from the people I love. That would be a dreadful way to behave, especially now. Being completely devoted to her means I'm fully present and engaged with what truly matters, doesn't it? That's the exact opposite of being distant, I should think. I hope you can see that I'm just trying to keep my heart exactly where it belongs right now. That makes sense, doesn't it?
Do you often find yourself worrying about your wife's health or your ability to care for her?

Worrying? Well, I... I suppose I do think about her health quite a bit, yes. But I wouldn't call it worrying, exactly. That sounds so... so frantic, doesn't it? Like I'm wringing my hands all day, and I certainly wouldn't want you to think I'm falling apart like that. 

It's more just... being attentive, really. I like to make sure she has everything she needs, and naturally, I want to be certain I'm doing things the right way for her. It's just normal concern, isn't it? Any devoted husband would want to make sure he's up to the task of caring for his wife after something like this. 

I mean, I'm perfectly capable, of course! I wouldn't want you to doubt my ability to look after her. I just... I just want to do a good job. That's a perfectly reasonable way to feel, wouldn't you say? It just shows how much I care, doesn't it?
Are there activities that you used to find pleasurable but no longer enjoy?

Oh, goodness, no. No, I still very much enjoy all my usual hobbies. I wouldn't want you to think I've lost interest in life or anything dreadful like that! 

I still absolutely love my history biographies and... well, tending to the roses out back. It's just that, at the moment, I haven't really had the time to sit down with a good book or get out into the yard. My focus has to be on my wife's recovery, naturally. But the enjoyment is certainly still there, I promise you! 

I've just put those little pleasures on the back burner for a little while until she's back on her feet. That’s just being responsible, isn't it? You wouldn't expect a good husband to be out playing around in the garden when she needs him inside, would you? So, no, I haven't stopped enjoying things at all. I'm just prioritizing, which is exactly what I should be doing, don't you agree?
Do you feel guilty about not being able to prevent your wife's fall?

Guilty? Oh, my... no, I wouldn't say guilty. I mean, I certainly wish it hadn't happened, of course! Any loving husband would. But... well, I was in the other room when she slipped. There really wasn't anything I could have done to catch her in time. 

I would absolutely hate for you to think I was being careless or negligent with her safety. I'm always so very careful with her! It was just a dreadful accident, plain and simple. You don't think I should feel guilty, do you? I mean, I've just been trying to focus all my energy on helping her get better now, rather than dwelling on the fall itself. That's the most constructive way to handle things, wouldn't you agree? It's much better to look forward and be supportive, isn't it?
Do you feel a persistent sense of sadness inside, even when you're trying to stay positive for your wife?

Sadness? Oh, my, no. I wouldn't use that word at all. I mean... naturally, it’s not exactly a joyful situation, having her laid up like this. But a persistent sadness? No, I certainly wouldn't want you to think I'm moping about the house or feeling sorry for myself. That wouldn't be very helpful to her recovery, would it? 

I try to keep a very positive outlook for both our sakes. A stiff upper lip, as they say. If I'm cheerful and optimistic, it helps her stay cheerful, and that's really the best medicine, don't you think? So, no, no deep sadness here inside. Just... determination to see her well again. That's the right attitude to have, isn't it? You don't think I'm handling this the wrong way, do you?
Have you noticed any change in your appetite since your wife's fall?

Appetite? Oh, no, not really. I mean, I'm certainly still eating! I wouldn't want you to think I'm neglecting myself or wasting away. That wouldn't be very responsible of me, would it? I need to keep my strength up to take care of my wife!

I suppose... well, maybe I haven't been making quite as many of those big, elaborate meals we used to have. But that's just because it seems a bit silly to go to all that trouble just for myself, with her eating mostly soup and toast right now. It's much more practical to just have something quick and simple, don't you agree? So, my appetite is perfectly fine, really. I'm just eating more efficiently, I suppose you could say. That makes sense under the circumstances, doesn't it?
Do you find yourself frequently preoccupied with worries about the future?

Preoccupied? Oh, goodness, no. I wouldn't say that at all. I mean... naturally, one has to think about practical things, especially with her recovery and making sure we have everything we need. But I'm certainly not sitting around wringing my hands or letting anxiety get the better of me. I really wouldn't want you to think I'm falling apart or losing my grip on things! 

I think it's much more productive to just take things one day at a time. Focus on the immediate tasks, you know? Managing the daily routine keeps the mind occupied in a healthy, useful way. That's the most sensible approach, wouldn't you say? You don't think I'm being short-sighted by just focusing on today, do you? I just feel like staying steady and grounded in the present is the best way I can be a reliable support for her right now. That's what a good husband ought to do, isn't it?
Do you find yourself frequently feeling on edge or nervous?

On edge? Oh, goodness, no. I wouldn't say that. I mean... naturally, one has to be a bit more attentive these days, keeping an ear out just in case she needs me from the other room. But nervous? No, I certainly wouldn't want you to think I'm pacing the floors or jumping at shadows. That would create a terribly stressful environment for her recovery, wouldn't it? 

I try very hard to maintain a calm, soothing presence in the house. A peaceful atmosphere is so important for healing, don't you agree? So I just focus on being a steady hand for her. I'm not really a high-strung sort of person anyway. You don't think I come across as anxious, do you? I really do believe staying perfectly composed is the best way I can serve her right now.
Do you often have trouble calming down once you start feeling upset or anxious?

Trouble calming down? Oh, no, not really. I mean, I'm a very rational person, you know? With my background, I've always been used to thinking things through logically. So if I ever do feel a bit... well, a bit overwhelmed, I just remind myself of the facts. There's no sense in letting emotions run away with you, is there? 

I wouldn't want you to think I'm the sort of person who throws tantrums or loses control. That wouldn't be very helpful to my wife at all, would it? She needs me to be the stable one. So if I ever feel a little flutter of worry, I just take a deep breath, maybe make a cup of tea, and get right back to whatever needs doing. It's much better to just stay practical and level-headed, don't you think? You don't see me as someone who gets easily flustered, do you? I really try my best to keep everything running smoothly.
Have you stopped enjoying or participating in any hobbies or activities that you previously found pleasurable since your wife's fall?

Hobbies? Well... I suppose I have stepped back from a few things, yes. But certainly not because I've lost interest! It's just... well, a matter of priorities, isn't it? I used to be quite involved with some mentoring programs, and I had my regular community commitments... and, well, I haven't exactly been showing up for those lately. But I'm sure they understand. Family has to come first right now, don't you agree? 

Though, I suppose... if I'm being perfectly honest with you... I wouldn't want you to think I'm completely dropping the ball, but... some of the practical things are getting just a bit difficult to keep on top of. Things I used to handle without even thinking about it—sorting the bills, the general home upkeep, just our basic household routines... they are, well, they're slipping badly right now. 

It’s terribly embarrassing to admit. A man with my education and background ought to be able to keep his own house in order, shouldn't he? But... it's only natural that a few chores might slide when you're dedicating all your time and energy to your wife's recovery, wouldn't you say? You don't think less of me for letting the paperwork pile up a bit, do you? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by focusing on her.
Do you find that you no longer take pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?

Take pleasure? Oh, heavens no, I wouldn't say that at all. I still very much enjoy the things I've always loved. If I had the time to sit down with a good history biography right now, I'm sure I would find it just as fascinating as ever. 

It's really just a matter of... well, not having the proper moment for it, rather than losing the joy itself. I wouldn't want you to worry that I'm becoming, oh, dreary or despondent or anything like that. That wouldn't be very good for my wife's morale, would it? I still have a wonderful capacity for enjoyment. It's just that right now, making sure she is comfortable and cared for... well, that brings me the most satisfaction. That's the right way to look at it, don't you think? You don't think it's unusual to just put personal amusements on the back burner for a little while, do you?
